fundamentals.definition: The golden hierarchy of editing priorities defined by legendary editor Walter Murch: 1) Emotion (51%), 2) Story (23%), 3) Rhythm (10%), 4) Eye-trace (7%), 5) 2D Plane of Screen (5%), 6) 3D Spatial Continuity (4%).
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Never sacrifice emotion or story rhythm just to preserve spatial continuity.

fundamentals.definition: A psychological film phenomenon where viewers derive more meaning from the interaction of two sequential shots than from a single shot in isolation (e.g. actor's neutral expression + bowl of soup = hunger; actor + coffin = grief).
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Demonstrates that the context of a cut shapes viewer emotion more than the clip itself.

fundamentals.definition: The exact length of time a single continuous camera take remains on screen before cutting.
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Shorter durations (< 3s) create tension, energy, or confusion; longer durations (> 7s) establish calm, drama, or focus.

fundamentals.definition: The rhythm and temporal speed at which scenes and cuts progress throughout a video sequence.
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Good pacing matches visual cuts to sound accents, narrative intent, and emotional beats.

fundamentals.definition: Maintaining consistent spatial, temporal, and action relationships across cuts (e.g., 180-degree rule, eyeline matching, matching action).
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Prevents jarring viewer disorientation unless intentionally broken for stylistic effect.

fundamentals.definition: Intentionally violating traditional continuity rules (jump cuts, spatial jumps) to shock, speed up time, or create psychological tension.
fundamentals.pacing_impact: High-energy pattern interrupt that grabs viewer attention.

fundamentals.definition: The structured timing of edits in relation to speech cadence, background music, or motion within the frame.
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Gives the edit a musical or pulse-like flow.

fundamentals.definition: Techniques used to bridge the gap between two separate video clips or scenes (Hard Cut, Dissolve, Wipe, Whip Pan, Fade).
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Dictates energy flow—hard cuts maintain momentum, fades signify passage of time, and whip pans create dynamic momentum.

fundamentals.definition: ProRes and DNxHR are intra-frame editing codecs (large files, light CPU load, smooth scrubbing). H.264/H.265 are inter-frame delivery codecs (compressed, heavy CPU load).
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Editing in ProRes or using proxies ensures zero lag during timeline playback and precise cutting.

fundamentals.term: Frame Rates (24 FPS vs 30 FPS vs 60 FPS)
fundamentals.definition: 24 FPS is cinema standard (filmic motion blur). 30 FPS is TV broadcast standard. 60 FPS / 120 FPS provides high temporal resolution, required for 25% smooth slow-motion ramping.
fundamentals.pacing_impact: Matching frame rates to intent preserves cinematic motion feel.
